name: Osmotic river-mouth power plant
effect: big molecules trapped behind a membrane draw water in
how: Where a river meets the sea, fresh water and seawater are separated by a membrane that lets water through but holds back salt. Water seeps across into the salty side and builds up pressure there, and the pressurised water spins a turbine and generator. It runs day and night on nothing but the saltiness difference.
why: Power from mixing fresh and salt water, using the pressure that draws water into cells.
